Before serving sprinkle with pepper [2].

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] V. Colocasia Antiquorum belonging to the dasheen or taro family, a valuable tuber, again mentioned in No. 172, 216, 244 and 322. Cf. various notes, principally that to No. 322. Also see U. S. Dept. of Agr. Farmer's Bulletin No. 1396, p. 2. This is a "new" and commercially and gastronomically important root vegetable, the flavor reminding of a combination of chestnuts and potatoes, popularly known as "Chinese potatoes" which has been recently introduced by the U. S. Government from the West Indies where it received the name, Dasheen, derived from de Chine--from China. [2] Tor. continues without interruption into the next formula.

recipes.title: Kurpitsa aleksandrialaiseen tapaan
recipes.originalTitle: Pumpkin, alexandrine style (ALITER CUCURBITAS MORE ALEXANDRINO)
recipes.description: Keitetty kurpitsa maustetaan pippurilla, kuminalla, korianterilla ja mintulla, ja päälle kaadetaan taateleista, pinjansiemenistä, hunajasta, etikasta ja garumista tehty kastike.
instructions: Keitä kurpitsa, purista vesi pois ja asettele vuokaan.
Ripottele päälle suola, pippuri, kumina, korianteri, minttu ja asafetida ja kostuta etikalla.
Survo taatelit ja pinjansiemenet hunajan, etikan ja kalakastikkeen kanssa, lisää siirappi ja öljy ja kaada kurpitsan päälle.
Kypsennä liemessä ja ripottele pippuria ennen tarjoilua.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText: Press the water out of the boiled pumpkin, place in a baking dish, sprinkle with salt, ground pepper, cumin, coriander seed, green mint and a little laser root; season with vinegar. Now add date wine and pignolia nuts ground with honey, vinegar and broth, measure out condensed wine and oil, pour this over the pumpkin and finish in this liquor and serve, sprinkle with pepper before serving.

recipes.title: Keitetty kurpitsa öljyssä ja garumissa
recipes.description: Kurpitsa haudutetaan kalakastikkeessa ja puhtaassa oliiviöljyssä.
instructions: Hauduta kurpitsaa kalakastikkeen, öljyn ja veden seoksessa pehmeäksi.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText: [boiled pumpkin] stewed in broth with pure oil.

recipes.title: Paistettu kurpitsa viinikastikkeella
recipes.description: Paistettu kurpitsa tarjotaan yksinkertaisen viinikastikkeen ja pippurin kanssa.
instructions: Paista kurpitsaviipaleet öljyssä kypsiksi.
Keitä viini ja kalakastike hetki kokoon ja kaada kurpitsan päälle. Ripottele pippuria.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText: [fried pumpkin served with] simple wine sauce and pepper.

recipes.title: Keitetty ja paistettu kurpitsa kuminaviinissä
recipes.originalTitle: Another way, boiled and fried (ALITER CUCURBITAS ELIXATAS ET FRICTAS)
recipes.description: Keitetty ja paistettu kurpitsa haudutetaan vuoassa kuminalla maustetun viinin ja öljyn kanssa.
instructions: Keitä kurpitsa ja paista se kevyesti.
Asettele vuokaan, kaada päälle kuminalla maustettu viini ja vähän öljyä ja kypsennä loppuun.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText: Boiled pumpkin fried is placed in a baking pan. Season with cumin wine, add a little oil; finish on the fire and serve.

recipes.title: Kurpitsamuhennos oreganolla ja sipulilla
recipes.description: Paistettu kurpitsa haudutetaan pippurin, lipstikan, kuminan, oreganon, sipulin, viinin ja garumin kanssa ja suurustetaan.
instructions: Paista kurpitsa öljyssä.
Lisää mausteet, sipuli, viini ja kalakastike ja hauduta vuoassa pehmeäksi.
Suurusta liemi (tai muussaa) ja tarjoa samassa vuoassa.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Fried [1] pumpkin, seasoned with pepper, lovage, cumin, origany, onion, wine broth and oil: stew the pumpkin [in this] in a baking dish, tie the liquid with roux [mash] and serve in the dish.

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] V. Baking the fruit reduces the water contents, renders the purée more substantial. G.-V. Tritas--mashed. Tor. connects tritas up with pepper, hence it is doubtful whether this dish of pumpkin is mashed pumpkin.

recipes.title: Kana ja kurpitsa persikoilla ja yrteillä
recipes.description: Kana ja kurpitsa haudutetaan yhdessä persikoiden ja sienten kanssa; mausteina pippuri, kumina, asafetida ja tuoreet yrtit, viini, öljy ja etikka.
instructions: Ruskista kanapalat öljyssä pata-astiassa.
Lisää kurpitsa, persikat, sienet, mausteet, viini ja etikka ja hauduta, kunnes kana on kypsää.
Lisää tuoreet yrtit lopuksi.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
[stew the pumpkin with a hen, garnish with] hard-skinned peaches, truffles; pepper, carraway, and cumin, silphium and green herbs, such as mint, celery, coriander, pennyroyal, cress, wine [1] oil and vinegar.

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] Tor. Vinum vel oleum; List. vinum, mel, oleum.

recipes.title: Sitruuna minttu-asafetidakastikkeessa
recipes.description: Sitruunahedelmä maustetaan vuoriselleillä, asafetidalla, kuivatulla mintulla, etikalla ja garumilla.
instructions: Viipaloi sitruunat ohuiksi.
Sekoita mausteet, etikka ja kalakastike ja kaada viipaleiden päälle. Tarjoa lisukkeena.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
For the preparation of citron fruit we take siler [2] from the mountains, silphium, dry mint, vinegar and broth.

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] List. Citrini--a lemon or cucumber squash. [2] Tor. Silerem; List. sil, which is hartwort, a kind of cumin or mountain fennel.

recipes.title: Haudutetut kurkut
recipes.description: Kuoritut kurkut haudutetaan liemessä tai viinikastikkeessa – mureita ja helposti sulavia.
instructions: Hauduta kurkkupaloja liemessä tai viinissä pehmeiksi, noin 10 minuuttia.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
[stew the] peeled cucumbers either in broth [1] or in a wine sauce; [and] you will find them to be tender and not causing indigestion.

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] Usually cucumbers are parboiled in water and then finished in broth; most often after being parboiled they are stuffed with forcemeat and then finished in broth.

recipes.title: Kurkut aivojen ja kuminan kanssa
recipes.description: Kuoritut kurkut haudutetaan keitettyjen aivojen, kuminan ja hunajan kanssa; kastike sidotaan munilla.
instructions: Hauduta kurkut paloina aivojen, kuminan, hunajan, sellerinsiementen, kalakastikkeen, öljyn ja veden kanssa.
Sido kastike vatkatuilla munilla miedolla lämmöllä.
Ripottele pippuria ja tarjoa.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
[peeled cucumbers are] stewed with boiled brains, cumin and a little honey. Add some celery seed, stock and oil, bind the gravy with eggs [1] sprinkle with pepper and serve.

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] Tor. bis obligabis--tie twice--for which there is no reason, except in case the sauce should curdle. List. oleo elixabis--fry in oil--obviously wrong, as the materials for this stew are already cooked. Sch. ovis obligabis--bind with eggs--which is the thing to do in this case.

recipes.title: Kurkkusalaatti polei-hunajakastikkeessa
recipes.description: Kurkkua pippurin, polein (tai mintun), hunajan, garumin ja etikan kanssa – välillä ripaus asafetidaa.
instructions: Sekoita mausteet, hunaja, kalakastike ja etikka.
Kaada kurkkuviipaleiden päälle ja tarjoa.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Cucumbers, pepper, pennyroyal, honey or condensed must, broth and vinegar; once in a while one adds silphium.

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

Sounds like a fancy dressing for raw sliced cucumbers, though there are no directions to this effect.

recipes.title: Meloni polei-hunajakastikkeessa
recipes.description: Meloni pippurin, polein, hunajan, garumin ja etikan kanssa – roomalainen makea-suolainen alkupala.
instructions: Sekoita mausteet, hunaja, kalakastike ja etikka.
Kaada melonipalojen päälle ja tarjoa.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Pepper, pennyroyal, honey or condensed must, broth and vinegar; once in a while one adds silphium.

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

Same as 84; which confirms above theory. It is quite possible that melons were eaten raw with this fancy dressing. Many people enjoy melons with pepper and salt, or, in salad form with oil and vinegar. Gourds, however, to be palatable, must be boiled and served either hot or cold with this dressing.

recipes.title: Malvanlehdet garumissa ja öljyssä
recipes.description: Pienet malvanlehdet garumin, öljyn ja etikan kanssa, isot viinikastikkeessa pippurin ja makean viinin kera.
instructions: Keitä lehdet nopeasti ja valuta.
Mausta kalakastikkeella, öljyllä ja etikalla – tai isommat lehdet makealla viinillä, pippurilla ja kalakastikkeella.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
The smaller mallows [are prepared] with garum [1], stock [2] oil and vinegar; the larger mallows [prepare] with a wine sauce, pepper and stock, [adding] condensed wine or raisin wine.

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] Tor. Garum; List. Oenogarum. [2] Liquamen--depending upon the mode of serving the mallows, hot or cold.

recipes.title: Kaalinversot kuminalla ja yrteillä
recipes.description: Keitetyt kaalin versot maustetaan kuminalla, suolalla, viinillä ja öljyllä, halutessa pippurilla, lipstikalla, mintulla ja korianterilla.
instructions: Keitä versot kypsiksi ja valuta.
Mausta kuminalla, suolalla, viinillä ja öljyllä, halutessasi myös pippurilla ja yrteillä.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
[boil the] sprouts; [1] [season with] cumin [3], salt, wine and oil; if you like [add] pepper, lovage, mint, rue, coriander; the tender leaves of the stalks [stew] in broth; wine and oil be the seasoning.

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] Including, perhaps, cauliflower and broccoli. [2] List. Cimæ & Coliculi. Nunc crudi cum condimentis nunc elixati inferentur. Served sometimes raw with dressing, sometimes boiled. [3] Cumin or carraway seed is still used today in the preparation of the delicious "Bavarian" cabbage which also includes wine and other spices.

recipes.title: Kaalinvarret ja muussatut lehdet
recipes.description: Halkaistut kaalinvarret keitetään; lehdet muussataan korianterin, sipulin, kuminan, pippurin ja makean viinin kanssa.
instructions: Halkaise varret ja keitä ne lehtien kanssa.
Muussaa lehdet ja mausta sipulilla, korianterilla, kuminalla, pippurilla, makealla viinillä ja öljyllä.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Cut the stalks in half and boil them. The leaves are mashed and seasoned with coriander, onion, cumin, pepper, raisin wine, or condensed wine and a little oil.

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

Very sensible way of using cabbage stalks that are usually thrown away. Note the almost scientific procedure: the stalks are separated from the leaves, split to facilitate cooking; they are cooked separately because they require more time than the tender greens. Our present method appears barbarous in comparison. We quarter the cabbage head, and either boil it or steam it. As a result either the tender leaves are cooked to death or the stems are still hard. The overcooked parts are not palatable, the underdone ones indigestible. Such being the case, our boiled cabbage is a complete loss, unless prepared the Apician way.

recipes.title: Kaalinvarret purjolla ja korianterilla
recipes.description: Keitetyt kaalinvarret vuokaan garumin ja öljyn kanssa, päälle kuminaa, pippuria, purjoa ja tuoretta korianteria.
instructions: Keitä varret ja asettele vuokaan.
Kostuta kalakastikkeella ja öljyllä, ripottele päälle kumina, pippuri, purjo ja korianteri ja lämmitä.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
The cooked [1] stalks are placed in a [baking] dish; moisten with stock and pure oil, season with cumin, sprinkle [2] with pepper, leeks, cumin, and green coriander [all] chopped up.

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] Tor. Coliculi assati--sauté, fried; (Remember: Choux de Bruxelles sauté) List. elixati--boiled. G.-V. Cauliculi elixati. [2] Tor. Superasperges; G.-V. piper asperges. Sounds like a salad of cooked cabbage. The original leaves us in doubt as to the temperature of the dish.

recipes.title: Kaalinversot purjon kanssa
recipes.description: Edellisten tapaan maustetut kaalinversot haudutetaan ryöpättyjen purjojen kanssa.
instructions: Ryöppää purjot ja versot.
Hauduta yhdessä kuminan, suolan, öljyn ja viinin kanssa.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText: The vegetable, seasoned and prepared in the above way is stewed with parboiled leeks.

recipes.title: Kaalinversot vihreiden oliivien kanssa
recipes.description: Maustetut kaalinversot lämmitetään vihreiden oliivien kanssa.
instructions: Keitä versot ja mausta kuminalla, öljyllä ja viinillä.
Lisää oliivit ja lämmitä yhdessä.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText: To the sprouts or stalks, seasoned and prepared as above, are added green olives which are heated likewise.

recipes.title: Kaalinversot speltin, pinjansiementen ja rusinoiden kanssa
recipes.description: Maustetut kaalinversot peitetään keitetyllä speltillä ja pinjansiemenillä, päälle rusinoita.
instructions: Keitä versot ja mausta kuminalla ja öljyllä.
Peitä keitetyllä speltillä ja pinjansiemenillä ja ripottele päälle rusinat.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Prepare the sprouts in the above way, cover them with boiled spelt and pine nuts [1] and sprinkle [2] with raisins.

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] The nuts should not astonish us. The French today have a delicious dish, Choux de Bruxelles aux Marrons--Brussels Sprouts with Chestnuts. Sprouts and chestnuts are, of course, cooked separately; the lightly boiled sprouts are sauté in butter; the chestnuts parboiled, peeled, and finished in stock with a little sugar or syrup, tossed in butter and served in the center of the sprouts. The Apician formula with cereal and raisins added is too exotic to suit our modern taste, but without a question is a nutritious dish and complete from a dietetic point of view. [2] Tor. Superasperges; G.-V. piper asperges.

recipes.title: Haudutetut purjot
recipes.description: Purjot keitetään suolalla vedessä ja öljyssä ja haudutetaan sitten öljyssä ja parhaassa garumissa.
instructions: Keitä purjot suolalla maustetussa vedessä, johon on lisätty loraus öljyä.
Valuta ja hauduta purjot loppuun öljyssä ja kalakastikkeessa.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Well matured leeks [1] are boiled with a pinch of salt [2] in [combined] water and oil [3]. They are then stewed in oil and in the best kind of broth, and served.

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] Tor. Poros bene maturos; G.-V. maturos fieri. [2] One of the rare instances where Apicius mentions salt in cookery, i.e., salt in a dry form. Pugnum salis--a fist of salt--he prescribes here. Usually it is liquamen--broth, brine--he uses. [3] Tor. is correct in finishing the sentence here. G.-V. continue et eximes., which is the opening of the next sentence, and it makes a difference in the formula.

recipes.title: Purjot kaalinlehtikääreissä
recipes.originalTitle: Another way to cook leeks (ALITER PORROS)
recipes.description: Keitetyt purjot kääritään kaalinlehtiin ja haudutetaan öljyssä ja garumissa.
instructions: Keitä purjot suolavedessä.
Kääri ne ryöpättyihin kaalinlehtiin ja hauduta öljyssä ja kalakastikkeessa.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Wrap the leeks well in cabbage leaves, having first cooked them as directed above [1] and then finish them in the above way.

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] Tor. in primis--first; List., G.-V. in prunis--hot embers.

recipes.title: Purjot laakerinmarjoilla
recipes.description: Purjot keitetään laakerinmarjojen kanssa ja tarjotaan öljyn ja garumin kera.
instructions: Keitä purjot laakerin kanssa.
Hauduta öljyssä ja kalakastikkeessa ja tarjoa.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Cook the leeks with [laurel] berries [1], [and otherwise treat them] and serve as above.

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] Tor. Porros in bacca coctos; List. in cacabo--cooked in a casserole; Sch. bafa embama--steeped, marinated (in oil); G.-V. in baca coctos. Another way to read this: baca et fabæ--with beans--is quite within reason. The following formula, 96, is perhaps only a variant of the above. Brandt: with olives, referring to No. 91 as a precedent.

recipes.title: Purjot ja vihreät pavut
recipes.description: Vihreät pavut keitetään purjojen keitinliemessä, josta ne saavat hyvän maun, ja tarjotaan purjojen kanssa.
instructions: Keitä purjot suolavedessä ja nosta pois.
Keitä pavut samassa liemessä kypsiksi.
Tarjoa yhdessä öljyn kanssa.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
After having boiled the leeks in water, [green string] beans which have not yet been prepared otherwise, may be boiled [in the leek water] [1] principally on account of the good taste they will acquire; and may then be served with the leeks.

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] Apicius needed no modern science of nutrition to remind him of the value of the mineral salts in vegetables.

recipes.title: Punajuuret korianterilla ja kuminalla
recipes.description: Viipaloidut punajuuret ja purjot keitetään korianterin, kuminan ja makean viinin kanssa; tarjotaan ilman lientä öljyn ja etikan kera.
instructions: Keitä punajuuret ja purjo murskattujen mausteiden, viinin ja veden kanssa kypsiksi.
Nosta punajuuret liemestä ja tarjoa öljyn ja etikan kanssa.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
TO MAKE A DISH OF BEETS THAT WILL APPEAL TO YOUR TASTE [1] SLICE [the beets, [2] with] LEEKS AND CRUSH CORIANDER AND CUMIN; ADD RAISIN WINE [3], BOIL ALL DOWN TO PERFECTION: BIND IT, SERVE [the beets] SEPARATE FROM THE BROTH, WITH OIL AND VINEGAR.

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] Sentence in Tor.; wanting in List. et al. [2] List. No mention of beets is made in this formula; therefore, it may belong to the foregoing leek recipes. V. This is not so. Here the noun is made subject to the first verb, as is practiced frequently. Moreover, the mode of preparation fits beets nicely, except for the flour to which we object in note 3, below. To cook beets with leeks, spices and wine and serve them (cold) with oil and vinegar is indeed a method that cannot be improved upon. [3] Tac., Tor., List., G.-V. uvam passam, Farinam--raisins and flour--for which there is no reason. Sch. varianam--raisin wine of the Varianian variety; Bas. Phariam. V. inclined to agree with Sch. and Bas.

recipes.title: Punajuuret sinapinsiemenillä
recipes.description: Punajuuret keitetään sinapinsiementen kanssa ja tarjotaan öljy-etikkakastikkeessa.
instructions: Keitä punajuuret sinapinsiementen kanssa kypsiksi.
Kuori ja viipaloi ja marinoi öljyssä ja etikassa.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Cook the beets with mustard [seed] and serve them well pickled in a little oil and vinegar.

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

V. Add bay leaves, cloves, pepper grains, sliced onion and a little sugar, and you have our modern pickled beets.

recipes.title: Vihreät keittovihannekset öljyssä
recipes.description: Nipuiksi sidotut vihreät keitetään ja tarjotaan puhtaan oliiviöljyn kanssa – sopii myös paistetun kalan lisukkeeksi.
instructions: Sido vihannekset nipuiksi ja keitä suolavedessä.
Valuta ja tarjoa oliiviöljyn kanssa.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
[the greens] tied in handy bundles, cooked and served with pure oil; also proper with fried fish.

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] Tac. Olisera; Tor. Olifera (sev mauis olyra) Tor. is mistaken. Hum., List. Olisatra; (old Ms. note in our Hum. copy: "Alessandrina uulgò") from olusatrum--olus--pot herbs, cabbage, turnips. G.-V. Holisera, from holus, i.e. olus and from olitor one who raises pot herbs.

recipes.title: Nauriit kuminalla ja ruudalla
recipes.description: Keitetyt nauriit maustetaan runsaalla kuminalla, ripauksella ruutaa, asafetidalla, garumilla, rypälesiirapilla ja öljyllä.
instructions: Keitä nauriit pehmeiksi ja purista vesi pois.
Survo kumina ja ruuta, lisää asafetida, kalakastike, siirappi ja öljy.
Lämmitä nauriit kastikkeessa miedosti ja tarjoa.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
[turnips are] cooked [soft, the water is] squeezed [out; then] crush a good amount of cumin and a little rue, add parthican [1] laser or [2] vinegar, stock, condensed wine and oil [3] heat moderately and serve.

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] i.e. Persian laser; List. laser, Parthicum; (the comma makes a difference!) Sch. particum--a part. [2] Tac., Tor. vel acetum; List. G.-V. mel, acetum. Another comma; and "honey" instead of "or." V. We doubt this: the vinegar is an alternative, for it takes the place of the more expensive Persian laser (which was an essence of the laser root, often diluted with vinegar). [3] List., G.-V. oleum modice: fervere; Tor. & oleum, quæ modice fervere facias. Again note Lister's punctuation here and in the foregoing notes. The misplaced commas and colons raise havoc with the formulæ everywhere. Torinus, who in his preface complains that his authority has no punctuation whatsoever and thereby indicates that it must have been a very ancient copy, (at least prior to the 1503 Tac. ed.) is generally not far from the mark. It is also doubtful that the variants are by him, as is claimed by List. In this instance, indeed, Tor. is again correct.

recipes.title: Keitetyt nauriit öljyssä ja etikassa
recipes.description: Keitetyt nauriit tarjotaan öljyllä maustettuina, halutessa etikan kanssa.
instructions: Keitä nauriit kypsiksi.
Mausta öljyllä, suolalla ja halutessasi etikalla.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
[the turnips are] boiled, served dressed with oil, to which, if desired, you may add vinegar [2].

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] Tor. ad delitias--delightful. [2] V. Presumably served cold, as a salad; cf. No. 122.

recipes.title: Retiisit pippurilla
recipes.description: Retiisit runsaan pippurin kanssa – tai raastettuna pippurin ja suolaveden kanssa.
instructions: Pippuroi retiisit runsaasti.
Tai raasta retiisit ja sekoita pippuriin ja kalakastikkeeseen.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Pepper the radishes well; or, equally well: grate it with pepper and brine.

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

Sch., G.-V. Rafanos; Raphanos agria,--a kind of horseradish; Plinius: h.e. raphanus sylvestris.

recipes.title: Kaalimuhennos kynteliällä ja sipulilla
recipes.description: Kaali keitetään yrttien kanssa, hienonnetaan ja maustetaan pippurilla, lipstikalla, kyntelillä, sipulilla, garumilla, öljyllä ja viinillä.
instructions: Keitä kaali yrttien kanssa pehmeäksi, purista vesi pois ja hienonna.
Survo mausteet ja sipuli, lisää kalakastike, öljy ja viini ja sekoita kaaliin. Lämmitä.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText: The cabbage is cooked with pot herbs in soda water; press [the water out] chop it very fine: [now] crush pepper, lovage, dry satury with dry onions, add stock, oil and wine.

recipes.title: Sellerimuhennos oreganolla
recipes.originalTitle: Another mashed green vegetable (ALTER OLUS MOLLE [EX APIO])
recipes.description: Keitetty selleri hienonnetaan ja haudutetaan pippurin, lipstikan, oreganon, sipulin, viinin, garumin ja öljyn kanssa.
instructions: Keitä selleri, purista vesi pois ja hienonna.
Survo mausteet ja sipuli, lisää viini, kalakastike ja öljy ja kuumenna.
Sekoita selleri kastikkeeseen.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Cook celery in soda water, squeeze [water out] chop fine. In the mortar crush pepper, lovage, origany, onion [and mix with] wine and stock, adding some oil. Cook this in the boiler [1] and mix the celery with this preparation.

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] in pultario. The pultarius is a pot in which cereals were boiled; from puls--porridge, pap.

recipes.title: Salaattimuhennos mintulla
recipes.originalTitle: Another mashed vegetable (ALITER OLUS MOLLE [EX LACTUCIS])
recipes.description: Salaatinlehdet keitetään sipulin kanssa, hienonnetaan ja maustetaan pippurilla, lipstikalla, sellerinsiemenellä ja mintulla.
instructions: Keitä salaatinlehdet ja sipuli nopeasti, purista vesi pois ja hienonna.
Survo mausteet, lisää kalakastike, öljy ja viini ja sekoita joukkoon.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText: Cook the lettuce leaves with onion in soda water, squeeze [the water out] chop very fine; in the mortar crush pepper, lovage, celery seed, dry mint, onion; add stock, oil and wine.

recipes.title: Villiyrtit salaattina tai keitettyinä
recipes.description: Pellon ja metsän yrtit joko salaattina garumin, öljyn ja etikan kanssa tai keitettyinä pippurin, kuminan ja mastiksin kera.
ingredients: 200 g syötäviä villiyrttejä (voikukka, nokkonen, vuohenputki, ketunleipä)
instructions: Salaatiksi: sekoita yrtit kalakastikkeeseen, öljyyn ja etikkaan.
Keitettynä: hauduta yrtit ja mausta pippurilla ja kuminalla.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Field and forest [1] herbs are prepared [2] [either raw] with stock [3] oil and vinegar [as a salad, [4]] or as a cooked dish [5] by adding pepper, cumin and mastich berries.

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] Tor. ac sylvestres; V. German, Feldsalat. [2] Tor. parantur; wanting in other editions. [3] Liquamine, here interpreted as brine. [4] Tac., Sch., et al. a manu; Tor. vel manu--because eaten with the hand. [5] Tor. vel in patina.

recipes.title: Endiivisalaatti sipulilla
recipes.description: Endiivit suolaveden, öljyn ja hienonnetun sipulin kanssa – talvella säilötyt endiivit hunajan tai etikan kera.
instructions: Leikkaa endiivit ja sekoita kalakastikkeeseen, öljyyn ja sipuliin.
Talvella (säilötyistä endiiveistä) mausta hunajalla tai etikalla.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Endives [are dressed] with brine, a little oil and chopped onion, instead of the real lettuce [1] in winter time the endives are taken out of the pickle [2] [and are dressed] with honey or vinegar.

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] Hum. pro lactucis uere; Tor. p. l. accipint; G.-V. p. l. vero (separated by period)--all indicating that endives are a substitute for lettuce when this is not available. [2] Cf. {Rx} No. 27, also Nos. 22 and 23.

recipes.title: Villisalaatti etikkakastikkeella
recipes.description: Villisalaatti etikkakastikkeen ja tilkan garumia kanssa – roomalaisten mukaan auttaa ruoansulatukseen.
instructions: Sekoita etikka, kalakastike ja öljy.
Kääntele salaatti kastikkeessa ja tarjoa.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
[dress it] with vinegar dressing and a little brine stock; which helps digestion and is taken to counteract inflation [2].

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] Tor. sic; Hum. agri l.; Tac. id.; Sch. and G.-V. have acri as an adjective to vinegar, the last word in the preceding formula. [2] List. and Hum. continuing: "And this salad will not hurt you"; but Tor., Sch. and G.-V. use this as a heading for the following formula.

recipes.title: Inkivääri-kuminaetikka salaatin jälkeen
recipes.description: Mausteetikka inkivääristä, ruudasta, taateleista, pippurista, hunajasta ja kuminasta – lusikallinen garumin kanssa aterian jälkeen.
instructions: Murskaa kumina ja sekoita kaikki aineet etikkaan. Anna uuttua muutama päivä ja siivilöi.
Sekoita pieni lusikallinen kalakastikkeeseen ja etikkaan ja nauti aterian jälkeen.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
[and in order that the lettuce may not hurt you take (with it or after it) the following preparation] [1] 2 ounces of ginger, 1 ounce of green rue, 1 ounce of meaty dates, 12 scruples of ground pepper, 1 ounce of good honey, and 8 ounces of either æthiopian or syrian cumin. Make an infusion of this in vinegar, the cumin crushed, and strain. Of this liquor use a small spoonful mix it with stock and a little vinegar: you may take a small spoonful after the meal [2].

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] Tac. and Tor. Ne lactucæ lædant [take it] cum zingiberis uncijs duabus, etc. Hum., List., G.-V. cumini unc. II. They and Sch. read the cum of Tac. and Tor. for cumini, overlooking the fact that the recipe later calls for Aethopian or Syrian cumin as well. This shifts the weights of the various ingredients from the one to the other, completely upsetting the sense of the formula. [2] Goll. ignores this passage completely. V. This is another of the medical formulæ that have suffered much by experimentation and interpretation through the ages. It seems to be an aromatic vinegar for a salad dressing, and, as such, a very interesting article, reminding of our present tarragon, etc., vinegars. To be used judiciously in salads. Again, as might be expected, the medicinal character of the formula inspires the medieval doctors to profound meditation and lively debate. Cf. {Rx} Nos. 34 and 108.

recipes.title: Kardonit munakastikkeessa
recipes.description: Kardonit suolaisen liemen, öljyn ja hienonnettujen kovaksi keitettyjen munien kanssa.
instructions: Keitä kardonit kypsiksi.
Kaada päälle kalakastike ja öljy ja ripottele hienonnetut munat pinnalle.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Cardoons [are eaten with a dressing of] briny broth, oil, and chopped [hard] eggs.

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

V. Precisely as we do today: French dressing and hard boiled eggs. We do not forget pepper, of course. Perhaps the ancient "briny broth" contained enough of this and of other ingredients, such as fine condiments and spices to make the dressing perfect.

recipes.title: Kardonit yrttikastikkeessa
recipes.description: Tuoreesta ruudasta, mintusta, korianterista ja fenkolista survottu kastike pippurin, lipstikan, garumin ja öljyn kanssa.
instructions: Keitä kardonit.
Survo yrtit hienoksi, lisää pippuri, lipstikka, kalakastike ja öljy.
Kaada kastike kardonien päälle.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Rue, mint, coriander, fennel--all green--finely crushed; add pepper, lovage, and [1] brine and oil [2].

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] Tac. and Tor. vel.; List., Sch., G.-V. mel--honey--which would spoil this fine vinaigrette or cold fines herbes dressing. However, even nowadays, sugar is quite frequently added to salad dressings. [2] Gollmer claims that this dressing is served with cooked cardoons, the recipe for which follows below. This is wanting in Tor.

recipes.title: Keitetyt kardonit kuminalla
recipes.description: Keitetyt kardonit pippurin, kuminan, garumin ja öljyn kanssa.
instructions: Keitä kardonit kypsiksi.
Mausta pippurilla, kuminalla, kalakastikkeella ja öljyllä.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText: [are served with] pepper, cumin, broth and oil.

recipes.title: Paistettu palsternakka viinikastikkeella
recipes.description: Paistetut juurekset (Vehlingin arvion mukaan karhunputken tai palsternakan juuria) yksinkertaisen viinikastikkeen kanssa.
instructions: Viipaloi palsternakat ja paista öljyssä kypsiksi.
Keitä viini ja kalakastike hetki kokoon ja kaada päälle.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Cow-parsnips are fried [and eaten] with a simple wine sauce.

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] Tac. Spondili uel fonduli and Sphon ...; Tor. as above; Hum. Spongioli uel funguli; List., id.; Sch. Sfondili uel funguli; G.-V. Sphondyli uel funduli. Cf. note to Nos. 46, 121, 122.

recipes.title: Palsternakka korianterilla ja pippurilla
recipes.description: Suolavedessä keitetty palsternakka puhtaan öljyn, tuoreen korianterin ja kokonaisten pippurien kanssa.
instructions: Keitä palsternakat suolavedessä.
Mausta öljyllä, korianterilla ja kokonaisilla pippureilla.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Boil the parsnips in salt water [and season them] with pure oil [1], chopped green coriander and whole pepper.

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] Tac. Oleo mero; Other editors: Oleo, mero. V. The comma is misplaced.

recipes.title: Palsternakka hunaja-ruutakastikkeessa
recipes.description: Keitetty palsternakka kastikkeessa, jossa sellerinsiementä, ruutaa, hunajaa, pippuria, makeaa viiniä ja garumia; suurustetaan.
instructions: Keitä palsternakat.
Sekoita kastikkeen aineet, kiehauta ja suurusta.
Lisää palsternakat, kuumenna ja ripottele pippuria.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText: Prepare the boiled parsnips with the following sauce: celery seed, rue, honey, ground pepper, mixed with raisin wine, stock and a little oil; bind this with roux [bring to a boiling point, immerse parsnips] sprinkle with pepper and serve.

recipes.title: Palsternakkasose korianterilla ja purjolla
recipes.description: Soseutettu palsternakka maustetaan kuminalla, ruudalla, garumilla, keitetyllä viinillä, öljyllä, korianterilla ja purjolla – sopii suolalihan kanssa.
instructions: Keitä palsternakat ja soseuta.
Sekoita joukkoon mausteet, kalakastike, siirappi, öljy, korianteri ja purjo.
Tarjoa suolatun sianlihan kanssa.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Mash the parsnips, [add] cumin, rue, stock, a little condensed wine, oil, green coriander [and] leeks and serve; goes well with salt pork [2].

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] Again faulty punctuation obscures the text. Carefully compare the following: Tac. and Tor. Spondylos teres, cuminum, etc. Hum., List. and G.-V. S. teres cuminum, i.e. crush the cumin. Sch. S. tores--dry, parch! [2] Inferes pro salso--serve with salt pork or bacon, or, instead of--Salsum--salt pork. Dann. Well seasoned with salt! Sch. infares pro salsa. For further confirmation of salsum cf. {Rx} Nos. 148-152.

recipes.title: Haudutettu palsternakka makeassa viinissä
recipes.description: Keitetty palsternakka haudutetaan öljyssä, garumissa, pippurissa ja makeassa viinissä; liemi suurustetaan.
instructions: Keitä palsternakat puolikypsiksi.
Hauduta kattilassa öljyn, kalakastikkeen, pippurin ja viinin kanssa.
Siivilöi liemi, suurusta ja kaada palsternakoiden päälle.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Boil the parsnips [sufficiently, if] hard [1] [then] put them in a sauce pan and stew with oil, stock, pepper, raisin wine, strain [2] and bind with roux.

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] Tor. præduratos; List. prædurabis. How can they be hardened? It may perhaps stand for "parboil." We agree with Tor. that the hard ones (præduratos) must be cooked soft. [2] Tor. and Tac. Colabis--strain; List. and G.-V. Colorabis--color. No necessity for coloring the gravy, but straining after the binding with roux is important which proves Tor. correct again. Cf. note 1 to {Rx} No. 73 and note 2 to {Rx} No. 55.

recipes.title: Paistettu palsternakka suolalla ja pippurilla
recipes.description: Palsternakka marinoidaan öljyssä ja garumissa tai paistetaan öljyssä; päälle suolaa ja pippuria.
instructions: Keitä palsternakat ja marinoi öljyssä ja kalakastikkeessa – tai paista ne öljyssä.
Ripottele suola ja pippuri ja tarjoa.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Finish [marinate] the parsnips in oil and broth, or fry them in oil, sprinkle with salt and pepper, and serve.

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] Ex G.-V. wanting in Tor. and List. Found in Sch. also. V. Procedure quite in accordance with modern practice. We envelope the p. in flour or frying batter.

recipes.title: Palsternakka-speltinyytit viinikastikkeessa
recipes.description: Keitetty palsternakka survotaan speltin ja munien kanssa, maustetaan pippurilla ja pinjansiemenillä, kääritään verkkorasvaan ja paistetaan.
instructions: Keitä palsternakat, poista sitkeät kuidut ja survo ne.
Sekoita spelttiin, muniin, kalakastikkeeseen, pippuriin ja pinjansiemeniin.
Muotoile pyöryköiksi, kääri verkkorasvaan ja paista. Tarjoa viinikastikkeessa.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Bruise the boiled parsnips [scallops, muscular part of shellfish] eliminate the hard strings; add boiled spelt and chopped hard eggs, stock and pepper. Make croquettes or sausage from this, adding pignolia nut and pepper, wrap in caul [or fill in casings] fry and serve them as an entrée dish in a wine sauce.

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] V. This formula is virtually a repetition of {Rx} No. 46, all the more bewildering because of the divergence of the term (Cf. {Rx} No. 115), which stands for "scallops" or the muscular part of any bivalve, at least in the above formula. The Græco-Latin word for cow-parsnip is spondylium, sphondylium, spondylion. It is almost certain that the preceding parsnips formulæ are in the right place here. They are in direct line with the other vegetables here treated--the shellfish--spondylus--would be out of place in this chapter, Book III, The Gardener. All the recipes, with the exception of the above, fit a vegetable like parsnips. Even Lister's and Humelberg's interpretation of the term, who read spongioli--mushrooms--could be questioned under this heading, Book III. It is barely possible that this entire series of formulæ, Spondyli uel fonduli ({Rx} Nos. 115-121) does belong to Book II among the scallop hysitia, though we are little inclined to accept this theory. Cf. {Rx} No. 122 which appears to be a confirmation of the view expressed above.

recipes.title: Paistetut porkkanat viinikastikkeella
recipes.description: Paistetut porkkanat tai palsternakat viinikastikkeen kanssa.
instructions: Paista porkkanat öljyssä.
Keitä viini ja kalakastike kokoon ja kaada päälle.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Carrots or parsnips are fried [and served] with a wine sauce.

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

V. Exactly like {Rx} No. 115, which may be a confirmation that spondyli stands for cow-parsnips.

recipes.title: Porkkanat öljyssä ja etikassa
recipes.description: Suolalla keitetyt porkkanat puhtaan öljyn ja etikan kanssa.
instructions: Keitä porkkanat suolavedessä.
Mausta öljyllä ja etikalla.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
The carrots [are cooked] salted [and served] with pure oil and vinegar.

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

V. As a salad. "Italian Salad" consists of a variety of such cooked vegetables, nicely dressed with oil and vinegar, or with mayonnaise. Cf. {Rx} No. 102.

recipes.title: Kuminaporkkanat
recipes.description: Keitetyt porkkanaviipaleet haudutetaan kuminan ja öljyn kanssa – keitinliemestä tehtiin kuminalientä vatsavaivaisille.
instructions: Keitä porkkanat ja viipaloi.
Hauduta kuminan ja öljyn kanssa ja suolaa.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
The carrots [are] boiled [and] sliced, stewed with cumin and a little oil and are served. At the same time [1] [here is your opportunity] make a cumin sauce [from the carrot juice] for those who have the colic [2].

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] Ex Tor. wanting elsewhere. [2] Tac. coliorum; Tor. cuminatum colicorum; List. c. coloratum--colored; G.-V. c. colorium.

recipes.title: Hyytelöity leipä-juustovuoka (salacattabia)
recipes.description: Kerroksittain liotettua leipää, juustoa, kurkkua, pinjansiemeniä, kapriksia ja kananmaksaa hyytelöidyssä liemessä – roomalainen kylmä alkuruoka.
instructions: Liota leipä vedessä ja purista kuivaksi.
Kerrosta vuokaan leipää, juustoja, kurkkua, pinjansiemeniä, kapriksia ja kananmaksaa.
Liuota liivate lämpimään liemeen ja kaada vuokaan niin, että kaikki peittyy. Hyydytä kylmässä ja kumoa.
Sekoita kastikkeen aineet ja tarjoa vuoan kanssa.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Pepper, fresh mint, celery, dry pennyroyal, cheese [3], pignolia nuts, honey, vinegar, broth, yolks of egg, fresh water, soaked bread and the liquid pressed out, cow's cheese and cucumbers are arranged in a dish, alternately, with the nuts; [also add] finely chopped capers [4], chicken livers [5]; cover completely with [a lukewarm, congealing] broth, place on ice [and when congealed unmould and] serve up [6].

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] Read: Pandectes--embracing the whole science. [2] Read: Salacaccabia--from salsa and caccabus--salt meat boiled in the pot. Sch. Sala cottabia; G.-V. cattabia. [3] Sch. casiam instead of caseum. [4] Sch. Copadiis porcinis--small bits of pork; List. cepas aridas puto--"shallots, I believe"; Lan. capparis; Vat., G.-V. id. [5] Dann. Chicken meat. [6] This dish if pork were added (cf. Sch. in note 4 above) would resemble our modern "headcheese"; the presence of cheese in this formula and in our word "headcheese" is perhaps not accidental; the cheese has been eliminated in the course of time from dishes of this sort while the name has remained with us. "Cheese" also appears in the German equivalent for custard--Eierkäse.

recipes.title: Apiciuksen hyytelövuoka
recipes.description: Leipää, kanaa, kateenkorvaa, juustoa, pinjansiemeniä, kurkkua ja salottisipulia hyytelöidyssä liemessä; päälle selleri-mintu-inkiväärikastike.
ingredients: 200 g kypsää kateenkorvaa tai lisää kanaa
instructions: Survo kastikkeen aineet sekaisin.
Kerrosta vuokaan leipää, kanaa, kateenkorvaa, juustoa, pinjansiemeniä, kurkkua ja salottisipulia.
Liuota liivate lämpimään liemeen, kaada vuokaan ja hyydytä kylmässä.
Kumoa vadille, valele kastikkeella ja tarjoa.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Put in the mortar celery seed, dry pennyroyal, dry mint, ginger, fresh coriander, seedless raisins, honey, vinegar, oil and wine; crush it together [in order to make a dressing of it]. [now] place 3 pieces of picentian bread in a mould, interlined with pieces of [cooked] chicken, [cooked] sweetbreads of calf or lamb, cheese [1], pignolia nuts, cucumbers [pickles] finely chopped dry onions [shallots] covering the whole with [jellified] broth. Bury the mould in snow up to the rim; [unmould] sprinkle [with the above dressing] and serve [2].

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] List. caseum Vestinum--a certain cheese from the Adriatic coast. [2] The nature of the first passage of this formula indicates a dressing for a cold dish. The dish was probably unmoulded when firm, and the jelly covered with this dressing, though the original does not state this procedure. In that case it would resemble a highly complicated chicken salad, such as we make today--mayonnaise de volaille en aspic, for instance. We recall the artistic molds for puddings and other dishes which the ancients had which were nicely suited for dishes such as the above. The Picentian bread--made of spelt--was a celebrated product of the bakeries of Picentia, a town of lower Italy, near the Tuscan sea, according to Pliny. Cf. {Rx} No. 141.

recipes.title: Täytetty leipä juusto-yrttitahnalla
recipes.description: Koverrettu leipä; sisus liotetaan viini-etikkaveteen ja sekoitetaan pippurin, hunajan, mintun, valkosipulin, korianterin ja suolaisen juuston kanssa.
instructions: Kovera leivän sisus, liota se veden, etikan ja viinin seoksessa ja purista.
Survo pippuri, hunaja, minttu, valkosipuli, korianteri, juusto, vesi ja öljy tahnaksi ja sekoita leivänsisukseen.
Täytä leipä tahnalla ja valele viinillä ennen tarjoilua.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Hollow out an alexandrine loaf of bread, soak the crumbs with posca [a mixture of water, wine, vinegar or lemon juice] and make a paste of it. Put in the mortar pepper, honey [1] mint, garlic, fresh coriander, salted cow's cheese, water and oil. Wine [2] poured over before serving [3].

Dishes of fish, vegetables, fruits and so forth patinæ piscium, holerum & pomorum

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] Wanting in Tor. [2] G.-V. insuper nivem--chilled on snow (like the preceding formula). Tac. insuper vinum; Sch. id. [3] A panada as is found in every old cookery book. Today it remains as a dressing for roast fowl, etc. Quoting from "A Collection of Receipts in Cookery, Physick and Surgery," London, 1724: "Panada for a Sick or Weak Stomach. Put the crumbs of a Penny White-Loaf grated into a Quart of cold Water, set both on the Fire together with a blade of Mace: When 'tis boil'd smooth, take it off the fire and put in a bit of Lemon-peel, the juice of a Lemon, a glass of Sack [Spanish Wine] and Sugar to your Taste. This is very Nourishing and never offends the Stomach. Some season with butter and Sugar, adding Currants which on some occasions are proper; but the first is the most grateful and innocent." Mrs. Glasse, a quarter century later, in her famous book [The Art of Cookery Made Plain and Easy, London, 1747, 1st ed.] omits the wine, but Mrs. Mason, at about the same time, insists on having it with panada. The imaginary or real relation between the sciences of cookery and medicine is illustrated here.

recipes.title: Arkinen aivovanukas
recipes.description: Haudutetut aivot survotaan pippurin, kuminan, asafetidan, garumin, keitetyn viinin, maidon ja munien kanssa ja kypsennetään vesihauteessa.
instructions: Survo aivot tahnaksi mausteiden, kalakastikkeen ja siirapin kanssa.
Sekoita joukkoon maito ja munat.
Kaada voideltuun vuokaan ja kypsennä vesihauteessa 160 asteessa noin 35 minuuttia.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Make a paste of stewed brains [calf's, pig's, etc.] season with pepper, cumin, laser, broth, thickened wine, milk and eggs [2] poach it over a weak fire or in a hot water [bath].

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] Tac. quottidiana; List. cottidiana. [2] List. ovis--with eggs, which is correct. Tor. holus; Lan. olus--herbs, cabbage. Cf. {Rx} No. 142.

recipes.title: Kumottava pähkinävanukas
recipes.originalTitle: Another dish, which can be turned over [a nut custard] (ALITER PATINA VERSATILIS)
recipes.description: Paahdetut saksan- ja hasselpähkinät survotaan hunajan kanssa ja sekoitetaan pippuriin, garumiin, maitoon, muniin ja öljyyn.
instructions: Paahda pähkinät ja survo ne hienoksi hunajan kanssa.
Sekoita joukkoon pippuri, kalakastike, maito, munat ja öljy.
Kaada voideltuun vuokaan, kypsennä vesihauteessa 160 asteessa noin 35 minuuttia ja kumoa jäähtyneenä.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
The dish, called turn-over, is thus made [1] crush very fine walnuts and hazelnuts [2] toast them and crush with honey, mix in pepper, broth, milk and eggs and a little oil [3].

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] Tor. [2] List. torres eas--toast them (wanting in Tor.) which is the thing to do. Cf. No. 143, practically a repetition of this. Cf. 301. [3] This laconic formula indicates a custard poached, like in the preceding, in a mould, which, when cooled off, is unmoulded in the usual way. This patina versatilis is in fact the modern crême renversée, with nuts. It is characteristic of Apicius for incompleteness and want of precise directions, without which the experiment in the hands of an inexperienced operator would result in failure.

recipes.title: Salaatinvarsivanukas
recipes.description: Salaatinvarret survotaan pippurin, garumin ja keitetyn viinin kanssa, keitetään ja sidotaan munilla.
instructions: Survo salaatti pippurin, kalakastikkeen ja siirapin kanssa, lisää vesi ja öljy ja keitä.
Sido vatkatuilla munilla miedolla lämmöllä.
Ripottele pippuria ja tarjoa.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Another dish is made of the [1] strunks of lettuce crushed with pepper, broth, thickened wine, [add] water and oil, and cook this; bind with eggs, sprinkle with pepper and serve [2].

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] Tor. [2] Very much like a modern soup, purée of lettuce.

recipes.title: Vihannes-aivovanukas
recipes.description: Keitetyt vihannekset ja aivot survotaan pippurin ja garumin kanssa, sekoitetaan kahdeksaan munaan, viiniin ja makeaan viiniin ja paistetaan.
instructions: Keitä vihannekset, jäähdytä ja valuta.
Survo pippuri kalakastikkeen kanssa, lisää aivot ja vihannekset ja survo tasaiseksi.
Sekoita munat, viini ja makea viini joukkoon ja maista.
Kaada hyvin öljyttyyn vuokaan ja paista 175 asteessa noin 35 minuuttia. Kumoa ja ripottele pippuria.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Take vegetables, clean and wash, shred [2] and cook them [3] cool them off and drain them. Take 4 [calf's] brains, remove [the skin and] strings and cook them [4] in the mortar put 6 scruples of pepper, moisten with broth and crush fine; then add the brains, rub again and meanwhile add the vegetables, rubbing all the while, and make a fine paste of it. Thereupon break and add 8 eggs. Now add a glassful [5] of broth, a glassful of wine, a glassful of raisin wine, taste this preparation. Oil the baking dish thoroughly [put the mixture in the dish] and place it in the hot plate, (that is above the hot ashes) [6] and when it is done [unmould it] sprinkle with pepper and serve [7].

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] List. frictilis; Vat. Ms. fusilis; G.-V. id.; Lan. frisilis. Patina frisilis remains unexplained. None of the various readings can be satisfactorily rendered. If the vegetables had remained whole the dish might be compared to a chartreuse, those delightful creations by the Carthusian monks who compelled by the strictest rules of vegetarianism evolved a number of fine vegetable dishes. On the other hand, the poached mixture of eggs and brains is akin to our farces and quenelles; but in modern cookery we have nothing just like this patina frisilis. [2] Wanting in List. [3] and [4] Wanting in Tor. [5] Cyathum. [6] Sentence in () ex Tor. [7] This and some of the following recipes are remarkable for their preciseness and completeness.

recipes.title: Kylmä parsavanukas pikkulinnuilla
recipes.originalTitle: Another cold asparagus [and figpecker] dish (ALITER PATINA DE ASPARAGIS FRIGIDA)
recipes.description: Parsasose sekoitetaan pippuriin, garumiin, viiniin, öljyyn ja kuuteen munaan; vuokaan asetellaan paistetut pikkulinnut ja päälle sose – tarjotaan kylmänä.
instructions: Survo parsa, ohenna vedellä ja siivilöi.
Kuumenna pippuri, kalakastike, viini ja öljy kattilassa.
Sekoita munat ja parsasose, lisää viiniseos ja sakeuta miedolla lämmöllä.
Asettele linnut voideltuun vuokaan, peitä soseella ja paista 175 asteessa noin 30 minuuttia. Jäähdytä, kumoa ja ripottele pippuria.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Cold asparagus pie is made in this manner [1] take well cleaned [cooked] asparagus, crush it in the mortar, dilute with water and presently strain it through the colander. Now trim, prepare [I.e. Cook or roast] figpeckers [2] [and hold them in readiness]. 3 [3] scruples of pepper are crushed in the mortar, add broth, a glass of wine, put this in a saucepan with 3 ounces of oil, heat thoroughly. Meanwhile oil your pie mould, and with 6 eggs, flavored with {oe}nogarum, and the asparagus preparation as described above; thicken the mixture on the hot ashes. Thereupon arrange the figpeckers in the mould, cover them with this purée, bake the dish. [when cold, unmould it] sprinkle with pepper and serve.

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] Tor. [2] Lan. and Tac. ficedulas curtas tres; Tor. curtas f.--three figpeckers cut fine. G.-V. F. curatas. Teres in ... (etc.)--Prepared F. [3] List. six; G.-V. id.

recipes.title: Parsavanukas korianterilla ja kynteliällä
recipes.originalTitle: Another asparagus custard (ALIA PATINA DE ASPARAGIS)
recipes.description: Parsankärjet survotaan pippurin, lipstikan, korianterin, kyntelin ja sipulin kanssa, ohennetaan viinillä, garumilla ja öljyllä ja sakeutetaan munilla.
instructions: Survo parsankärjet ja mausteet sipulin kanssa, ohenna viinillä, kalakastikkeella ja öljyllä.
Kaada voideltuun pannuun ja kuumenna. Lisää halutessasi vatkatut munat ja kypsennä keittämättä.
Ripottele hienoa pippuria.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Asparagus pie is made like this [1] put in the mortar asparagus tips [2] crush pepper, lovage, green coriander, savory and onions; crush, dilute with wine, broth and oil. Put this in a well-greased pan, and, if you like, add while on the fire some beaten eggs to it to thicken it, cook [without boiling the eggs] and sprinkle with very fine pepper.

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] Tor. [2] Reference to wine wanting in Tor. We add that the asparagus should be cooked before crushing.

recipes.title: Villivihannesvanukas
recipes.originalTitle: A dish of field vegetables (PATINA EX RUSTICIS)
recipes.description: Kuten parsavanukas, mutta villivihanneksista, timjamista, paprikasta, kurkusta tai versoista – halutessa luuttoman kalan tai kanan kanssa.
ingredients: 400 g vihanneksia (paprika, kurkku, nuoret versot tai villiyrtit)
instructions: Survo tai hienonna vihannekset mausteiden ja sipulin kanssa, ohenna viinillä, kalakastikkeella ja öljyllä.
Halutessasi asettele vuoan pohjalle kalaa tai kanaa.
Sekoita joukkoon vatkatut munat, kaada vuokaan ja paista 175 asteessa noin 30 minuuttia.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
By following the above instructions you may make [2] a pie of field vegetables, or of thyme [3] or of green peppers [4] or of cucumbers or of small tender sprouts [5] same as above, or, if you like, make one underlaid with boneless pieces of fish or of chicken [combined with any of the above vegetables] [6].

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] Tor. Patina ex oleribus agrestibus. [2] Tor. wanting in other texts. [3] Sch., G.-V. tamnis--wild wine; List. cymis cuminis; Lan., Tac. tinis; Vat. Ms. tannis. Thyme is hardly likely to be the chief ingredient of such a dish; the chances are it was used for flavoring and that the above enumerated vegetables were combined in one dish. [4] List., G.-V., Goll.--mustard; Dann. green mustard. Tor. sive pipere viridi--green peppers, which we accept as correct, gastronomically at least. [5] Goll., Dann. cabbage, the originals have coliculis--small tender sprouts on the order of Brussels sprouts or broccoli, all belonging to the cabbage family. [6] Pulpa--boneless pieces of meat, also fruit purée; pulpamentum--dainty bits of meat.

recipes.title: Seljanmarjavanukas
recipes.originalTitle: Elderberry custard or pie (PATINA DE SAMBUCO)
recipes.description: Keitetty seljanmarjasose maustetaan pippurilla, garumilla, viinillä ja makealla viinillä ja sakeutetaan munilla vesihauteessa – lämpimänä tai kylmänä.
instructions: Keitä marjat vedessä (raakoina ne ovat myrkyllisiä), kuori vaahto ja siivilöi.
Survo pippuri kalakastikkeen kanssa ja sekoita sosesoseeseen viinien ja öljyn kanssa.
Kuumenna vesihauteessa sekoittaen ja lisää vatkatut munat. Kun seos sakenee, ripottele pippuria ja tarjoa.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
A dish of elderberries, either hot or cold, is made in this manner [2] take elderberries [3] wash them; cook in water, skim and strain. Prepare a dish in which to cook the custard [4] crush 6 scruples of pepper with a little broth; add this to the elderberry pulp with another glass of broth, a glass of wine, a glass of raisin wine and as much as 4 ounces of oil. Put the dish in the hot bath and stir the contents. As soon as it is getting warm, quickly break 6 eggs and whipping them, incorporate them, in order to thicken the fluid. When thick enough sprinkle with pepper and serve up.

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] G.-V. Sabuco. [2] Tor. wanting in other texts. [3] Hum. semen de sambuco--E. seed. [4] List. Place the berries in a dish; to their juice add pepper, (etc.).

recipes.title: Ruusuvanukas
recipes.originalTitle: Rose pie, rose custard or pudding (PATINA DE ROSIS)
recipes.description: Ruusun terälehdistä survottu mehu sekoitetaan aivojen, pippurin, munien ja viinin kanssa ja kypsennetään vesihauteessa – Apiciuksen kuuluisa erikoisuus.
ingredients: 300 g keitettyjä aivoja tai 300 g tuorejuustoa
instructions: Poista terälehtien valkoiset tyvet, survo lehdet kalakastikkeen kanssa, lisää vesi ja siivilöi mehu.
Survo pippuri mehuun ja sekoita aivojen (tai juuston) kanssa tasaiseksi.
Lisää munat, viinit ja öljy.
Kaada voideltuun vuokaan ja kypsennä vesihauteessa 160 asteessa noin 35 minuuttia. Ripottele pippuria.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Take roses fresh from the flower bed, strip off the leaves, remove the white [from the petals and] put them in the mortar; pour over some broth [and] rub fine. Add a glass of broth and strain the juice through the colander. [this done] take 4 [cooked calf's] brains, skin them and remove the nerves; crush 8 scruples of pepper moistened with the juice and rub [with the brains]; thereupon break 8 eggs, add 1 [1] glass of wine, 1 glass of raisin wine and a little oil. Meanwhile grease a pan, place it on the hot ashes [or in the hot bath] in which pour the above described material; when the mixture is cooked in the bain maris [2] sprinkle it with pulverized pepper and serve [3].

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] List., G.-V. 1-1/2 glass. [2] Hot water bath. [3] Tor. continues {Rx} No. 135 without interruption or caption, and describes the above recipe. He reads: De thoris accipies rosas, but List. insists that de thoris be read de rosis; Lan., Tac. de toris; V. de thoris may be read "fresh from the flower bed." Cf. {Rx} Nos. 167 and 171 in which case the "rose" may stand for rosy apple, or "Roman Beauty" apple. "Rose apple" also is a small pimento, size of a plum.

recipes.title: Kurpitsavuoka kuminalla
recipes.description: Haudutettu ja soseutettu kurpitsa vuokaan, mausteeksi kuminaa ja öljyä, ja uuniin.
instructions: Hauduta kurpitsa pehmeäksi ja soseuta.
Mausta kuminalla, suolalla ja öljyllä, levitä vuokaan ja kuumenna uunissa.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
And pumpkin pie is made thus [2] stewed and mashed pumpkin is placed in the pan [or pie dish] seasoned with a little cumin essence. Add a little oil; heat [bake] and serve [3].

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] Dann. Cucumber Dish. [2] Tor. Wanting in other texts. [3] Modern English recipes for stewed pumpkin resemble this Apician precept, but America has made a really palatable dish from pumpkin by the addition of eggs, cinnamon, nutmeg, ginger--spices which the insipid pumpkin needs. The ancient original may have omitted the eggs because Apicius probably expected his formula to be carried out in accordance with the preceding formulæ. Perhaps this is proven by the fact that Tor. continues the Rose Pie recipe with et cucurbita patina sic fiet.

recipes.title: Pikkukalat valkoviinissä ruudan ja meiramin kanssa
recipes.originalTitle: Sprats or smelts au vin blanc (PATINA DE APUA)
recipes.description: Kuoret tai pikkukalat haudutetaan öljyssä, garumissa ja viinissä yrttinipun kanssa; päälle pippuria.
ingredients: 600 g kuoreita, muikkuja tai pieniä kalafileitä
instructions: Kääntele kalat öljyssä ja asettele matalaan pannuun.
Lisää öljy, kalakastike ja viini sekä yrttinippu ja hauduta kypsiksi.
Poista yrtit, mausta pippurilla ja tarjoa.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Clean the smelts [or other small fish, filets of sole, etc. Of white meat] marinate [I.e. Impregnate with] in oil, place in a shallow pan, add oil, broth [2] and wine. Bunch [3] [fresh] rue and marjoram and cook with the fish. When done remove the herbs, season the fish with pepper and serve [4].

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] Ex List. and G.-V. wanting in Tor. [2] Liquamen, which in this case corresponds to court bouillon, a broth prepared from the trimmings of the fish, herbs, and wine, well-seasoned and reduced. [3] Our very own bouquet garni, a bunch of various aromatic herbs, inserted during coction and retired before serving. [4] Excellent formula for fish in white wine, resembling our ways of making this fine dish. This again illustrates the laconic style of the ancient author. He omitted to say that the fish, when cooked, was placed on the service platter and that the juices remaining in the sauce pan were tied with one or two egg yolks, diluted with cream, or wine, or court bouillon, strained and poured over the fish at the moment of serving. This is perhaps the best method of preparing fish with white meat of a fine texture. Pink or darker fish do not lend themselves to this method of preparation.

recipes.title: Anjovisvanukas
recipes.originalTitle: Smelt pie, or, sprat custard (PATINA DE ABUA SIVE APUA)
recipes.description: Hienonnetut pikkukalat sekoitetaan pippurin, ruudan, garumin, öljyn ja munien kanssa ja höyrytetään hyytyväksi – ”kukaan ei arvaa, mitä syö”.
ingredients: 400 g kypsää pikkukalaa tai anjovista ruodottuna
instructions: Hienonna kala ja levitä vuokaan.
Sekoita mausteet, kalakastike, öljy ja munat ja kaada kalan päälle.
Kypsennä höyryssä tai vesihauteessa hyytyväksi keittämättä. Ripottele pippuria ja kanna pöytään.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Boneless pieces of anchovies or [other small] fish, either roast [fried] boiled, chop very fine. Fill a casserole generously with the same [season with] crushed pepper and a little rue, add sufficient broth and some oil, and mix in, also add enough raw eggs so that the whole forms one solid mass. Now carefully add some sea-nettles but take pain that they are not mixed with the eggs. Now put the dish into the steam so that it may congeal [but avoid boiling] [2]. When done sprinkle with ground pepper and carry into the dining room. Nobody will be able to tell what he is enjoying [3].

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] Tac., Tor. sic. List., G.-V. p. de apua sine apua--a dish of anchovies (or smelts) without anchovies. Tor. formula bears the title patina de apua, and his article opens with the following sentence: patin de abua sive apua sic facies. He is therefore quite emphatic that the dish is to be made with the abua or apua (an anchovy) and not without apua, as List. has it. Lan. calls the dish: P. de apabadiade, not identified. [2] Tor. impones ad uaporem ut cum ouis meare possint--warning, get along with the eggs, i.e. beware of boiling them for they will curdle, and the experiment is hopelessly lost. List. however, reads meare possint thus: bullire p.--boil (!) It is quite plain that Tor. has the correct formula. [3] et ex esu nemo agnoscet quid manducet. Dann. renders this sentence thus: "Nobody can value this dish unless he has partaken of it himself." He is too lenient. We would rather translate it literally as we did above, or say broadly, "And nobody will be any the wiser." List. dwells at length upon this sentence; his erudite commentary upon the cena dubia, the doubtful meal, will be found under the heading of cena in our vocabulary. List. pp. 126-7. List. undoubtedly made the mistake of reading sine for sive. He therefore omitted the apua from his formula. The above boastful sentence may have induced him to do so. The above is a fish forcemeat, now seldom used as an integral dish, but still popular as a dressing for fish or as quenelles. The modern fish forcemeat is usually made of raw fish, cream and eggs, with the necessary seasoning. The material is poached or cooked much in the same manner as prescribed by the ancient recipe.

recipes.title: Juhlava kerrosvuoka kanasta, makkarasta ja vihanneksista maitokastikkeessa
recipes.originalTitle: A rich entrée of fish, poultry and sausage in cream (PATINA EX LACTE)
recipes.description: Kerroksittain vihanneksia, kanaa, makkaraa, kovaksi keitettyjä munia, kalaa ja tuorejuustoa, päälle mausteinen maito-munaseos – roomalainen juhlavuoka.
instructions: Keitä vihannekset ja asettele ne vuoan pohjalle.
Kerrosta päälle kana, makkara, munanpuolikkaat, kala ja juusto. Ripottele väliin pinjansiemeniä ja kokonaisia pippureita.
Keitä jauhetut mausteet pienessä määrässä vettä, sekoita maitoon ja muniin ja kaada vuokaan.
Paista 175 asteessa noin 40 minuuttia, kunnes munamaito on hyytynyt.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Soak [pignolia] nuts, dry them, and also have fresh sea-urchins [1] ready. Take a deep dish [casserole] in which arrange the following things [in layers]: medium-sized mallows and beets, mature leeks, celery, stewed tender green cabbage, and other boiled green vegetables [2], a disjointed [3] chicken stewed in its own gravy, cooked [calf's or pig's] brains, lucanian sausage, hard boiled eggs cut into halves, big tarentinian sausage [4] sliced and broiled in the ashes, chicken giblets or pieces of chicken meat. Bits of fried fish, sea nettles, pieces of [stewed] oysters and fresh cheese are alternately put together; sprinkle in between the nuts and whole pepper, and the juice as is cooked from pepper, lovage, celery seed and silphium. This essence, when done, mix with milk to which raw eggs have been added [pour this over the pieces of food in the dish] so that the whole is thoroughly combined, stiffen it [in the hot water bath] and when done [garnish with] fresh mussels [sea-urchins, poached and chopped fine] sprinkle pepper over and serve.

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] Sea-urchins, wanting in Tor. [2] Sentence wanting in G.-V. [3] Pullum raptum, in most texts; G.-V. p. carptum--plucked. Of course! Should raptum be translated literally? A most atrocious way of killing fowl, to be sure, but anyone familiar with the habits of the ancients, particularly with those of the less educated element, should not wonder at this most bestial fashion, which was supposed to improve the flavor of the meat, a fashion which, as a matter of fact still survives in the Orient, particularly in China. [4] Vat. Ms. Tarentino farsos; Tor. cooks the sausage in the ashes--coctos in cinere; List. in cinere legendum jecinora--chicken giblets. Lister's explanation of the Tarentinian sausage is found in the vocabulary, v. Longano.

recipes.title: Apiciuksen lettuvuoka
recipes.description: Kalaa, kanaa ja pikkulintuja muhennoksena kerrostettuna ohuiden lettujen kanssa, päälle munaseos – roomalainen lasagnen sukulainen.
instructions: Pilko lihat ja kala tasaisiksi paloiksi.
Kiehauta pippuri, lipstikka, kalakastike, viini ja liemi, suurusta ja lisää palat. Kiehauta.
Kerrosta vuokaan lettuja ja muhennosta; ripottele väliin pinjansiemeniä ja pippureita. Viimeiseksi letku.
Vatkaa munat öljyn kanssa ja kaada pinnalle. Paista 175 asteessa noin 30 minuuttia ja ripottele pippuria.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
The apician dish is made thus: take small pieces of cooked sow's belly [with the paps on it] pieces of fish, pieces of chicken, the breasts of figpeckers or of thrushes [slightly] cooked, [and] whichever is best. Mince all this very carefully, particularly the figpeckers [the meat of which is very tender]. Dissolve in oil strictly fresh eggs; crush pepper and lovage, pour over some broth and raisin wine, put it in a saucepan to heat and bind with roux. After you have cut all in regular pieces, let it come to the boiling point. When done, retire [from the fire] with its juice of which you put some in another deep pan with whole pepper and pignolia nuts. Spread [the ragout] out in single layers with thin pancakes in between; put in as many pancakes and layers of meat as is required to fill the dish; put a final cover of pancake on top and sprinkle with pepper after those eggs have been added [which serve] to tie the dish. Now put this [mould or dish] in a boiler [steamer, hot water bath, allow to congeal] and dish it out [by unmoulding it]. An expensive silver platter would enhance the appearance of this dish materially.

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] Cf. {Rx} No. 126.

recipes.title: Arkinen lettuvuoka
recipes.description: Kypsiä lihan- ja kalanpaloja oreganolla maustetussa munakastikkeessa, kerrostettuna lettujen kanssa ja kumottuna vadille.
ingredients: 600 g kypsiä liha-, kana- ja kalapaloja
instructions: Survo mausteet ja sekoita kalakastikkeeseen, viineihin ja öljyyn. Sekoita vatkattuihin muniin ja sakeuta vesihauteessa.
Sekoita lihapalat munakastikkeeseen.
Kerrosta voideltuun vuokaan muhennosta ja lettuja, päällimmäiseksi hyvä letku. Tee keskelle höyryreikä.
Paista vesihauteessa 175 asteessa noin 30 minuuttia, kumoa ja ripottele pippuria.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Pieces of cooked sow's udder, pieces of cooked fish, chicken meat and similar bits, mince uniformly, season well and carefully [2]. Take a metal dish [for a mould]. Break eggs [in another bowl] and beat them. In a mortar put pepper, lovage and origany [3], which crush; moisten [this] with broth, wine, raisin wine and a little oil; empty it into the bowl [with the beaten eggs, mix] and heat it [in the hot water bath]. Thereupon when [this is] thickened mix it with the pieces of meat. Now prepare [alternately] layers of stew and pancakes, interspersed with oil [in the metal mould reserved for this purpose] until full, cover with one real good pancake [4], cut into it a vent hole for chimney on the surface [bake in hot water bath and when done] turn out upside down into another dish. Sprinkle with pepper and serve.

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] List. cottidiana; G.-V. cotidiana. Everyday Dish, in contrast to the foregoing Apician dish which is more sumptuous on account of the figpeckers or thrushes. In the originals these two formulæ are rolled into one. Cf. {Rx} No. 128. [2] G.-V. Hæc omnia concides; Tor. condies; List. condies lege concides which we dispute. Condies--season, flavor--is more correct in this place; concides--mince--is a repetition of what has been said already. [3] Origany wanting in G.-V. [4] List. superficie versas in discum insuper in superficium pones; Sch. a superficie versas indusium super focum pones; G.-V. in discum; Tor. unum uerò laganum fistula percuties à superficie uersas in discum in superficiem præterea pones--which we have translated literally above, as we believe Tor. to be correct in this important matter of having a chimney on top of such a pie.

recipes.title: Makea pähkinävanukas
recipes.originalTitle: Nut custard turn-over (PATINA VERSATILIS VICE DULCIS)
recipes.description: Paahdetut pinjansiemenet ja pähkinät survotaan hunajan kanssa ja kypsennetään maidon ja munien kanssa vesihauteessa.
instructions: Paahda pähkinät ja survo hunajan kanssa.
Vatkaa joukkoon pippuri, kalakastike, maito, munat ja öljy.
Kaada vuokiin ja kypsennä vesihauteessa 160 asteessa noin 35 minuuttia. Kumoa kylmänä.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Pignolia nuts, chopped or broken nuts [other varieties] are cleaned and roasted and crushed with honey. Mix in [beat well] pepper, broth, milk, eggs, a little honey [2] and oil. [thicken slowly on fire without boiling, fill in moulds, taking care that the nuts do not sink to the bottom, bake in hot water bath, when cold unmould].

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] Practically the only recipe in Apicius fairly resembling a modern "dessert." This is practically a repetition of {Rx} No. 129, which see. [2] Tor. modico melle; List. m. mero--pure wine and also pure honey, i.e. thick honey for sweetening. Wine would be out of place here. This is an excellent example of nut custard, if the "pepper" and the "broth" (liquamen), of the original, in other words spices and brine, or salt, be used very sparingly. For "pepper" nutmeg or allspice may be substituted, as is used today in such preparations. The oil seems superfluous, but it is taking the place of our butter. This very incomplete formula is characteristic because of the absence of weights and measures and other vital information as to the manipulation of the materials. None but an experienced practitioner could make use of this formula in its original state. Goll. adds toasted raisins, for which there is no authority. The text now proceeds without interruption to the next formula.

recipes.title: Suolakala-juustovuoka (tyrotarica)
recipes.description: Paistettu suolakala, kala ja kananmaksa sulatetun juuston kanssa vuokaan; päälle oregano-ruutakastike, joka sidotaan munilla, ja kuminaa.
ingredients: 300 g suolakalaa liotettuna (esim. suolasilli tai turska)
instructions: Paista suolakala öljyssä, poista ruodot ja revi palasiksi. Asettele vuokaan tuoreen kalan ja maksan kanssa ja peitä sulatetulla juustolla. Lämmitä.
Keitä mausteet, viinit ja öljy hiljalleen ja sido munilla.
Kaada kastike vuokaan, ripottele kumina ja tarjoa.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Take any kind of salt fish [3] cook [fry or broil it] in oil, take the bones out, shred it [and add] pieces of cooked brains, pieces of [other, fresh (?)] fish, minced chicken livers [4] and [cover with] hot soft [I.e. Liquefied] cheese. Heat all this in a dish; [meanwhile] grind pepper, lovage, origany, seeds of rue with wine, honey wine and oil; cook all on a slow fire; bind [this sauce] with raw eggs; arrange [the fish, etc.]. Properly [incorporate with the sauce] sprinkle with crushed cumin and serve [5].

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] G.-V., List., Vat. Ms. Thyrotarnica; cf. notes to {Rx} Nos. 427, 428. [2] Tor. [3] Tor. Wanting in other texts. [4] List., G.-V. here add hard boiled eggs, which is permissible, gastronomically. [5] Modern fish au gratin is made in a similar way. Instead of this wine sauce a spiced cream sauce and grated cheese are mixed with the bits of cooked fish, which is then baked in the dish. Brains, chicken, etc., too, are served au gratin, but a combination of the three in one dish is no longer practiced. However, the Italian method of baking fish, etc., au gratin à l'Italienne contains even more herbs and wine reduction than the above formula.

recipes.title: Suolakalapyörykät viinikastikkeessa
recipes.originalTitle: Salt fish balls in wine sauce (PATELLA ARIDA)
recipes.description: Liotettu suolakala hienonnetaan yrttien ja mausteiden kanssa pyöryköiksi, haudutetaan viinissä ja garumissa ja tarjotaan kyntelillä ja sipulilla maustetussa kastikkeessa.
instructions: Keitä kala, poista ruodot ja hienonna. Mausta yrteillä ja mausteilla, sido munalla ja muotoile pyöryköiksi.
Hauduta pyörykät viinissä, kalakastikkeessa ja öljyssä ja asettele vadille.
Lisää liemeen sipuli, kynteli ja etikka, keitä ja suurusta. Kaada pyöryköiden päälle ja ripottele timjamia ja pippuria.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
Dry pieces of salt tursio [3] are boned, cleaned [soaked in water, cooked] shredded fine and seasoned with ground pepper, lovage, origany, parsley, coriander, cumin, rue seeds and dry mint. Make fish balls out of this material and poach the same in wine, broth and oil; and when cooked, arrange them in a dish. Then make a sauce [utilizing the broth, the court bouillon in which the balls were cooked] season with pepper, lovage, satury, onions and wine and vinegar, also add broth and oil as needed, bind with roux [4] [pour over the balls] sprinkle with thyme and ground pepper [5].

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] Reminding us of the Norwegian fiske boller in wine sauce, a popular commercial article found canned in delicatessen stores. [2] List. patella sicca--dry, perhaps because made of dried fish. [3] List. isicia de Tursione; G.-V. Thursione. Probably a common sturgeon, or porpoise, or dolphin. List. describes it as "a kind of salt fish from the Black Sea; a malicious fish with a mouth similar to a rabbit"; Dann. thinks it is a sturgeon, but in Goll. it appears as tunny. The ancients called the sturgeon acipenser; but this name was gradually changed into styrio, stirio and sturio, which is similar to tursio (cf. styrio in the vocabulary). The fish in question therefore may have been sturgeon for which the Black Sea is famous. [4] List., G.-V. ovis obligabis--tie with eggs--certainly preferable to the Tor. version. [5] Tor. thyme. The above is an excellent way of making fish balls, it being taken for granted, of course, that the salt fish be thoroughly soaked and cooked in milk before shaping into balls. The many spices should be used very moderately, some to be omitted entirely. We read between the lines of the old formula that the Tursio had a long journey from Pontus to Rome; fish however dry acquires a notorious flavor upon such journeys which must be offset by herbs and spices. It is quite possible that the ancients made a réduction of the herbs and spices mentioned in this formula; in fact, the presence of vinegar leads us to believe this, in which case this formula would be nothing but a very modern sauce. The herbs and spices in a réduction are crushed and boiled down in vinegar and wine, and strained off, they leave their finest flavor in the sauce.

recipes.title: Vihannespata kynteliällä ja korianterilla
recipes.description: Ryöpätyt vihannekset haudutetaan pippurin, lipstikan, korianterin, kyntelin ja sipulin, viinin, garumin, etikan ja öljyn kanssa ja suurustetaan.
instructions: Ryöppää vihannekset, purista ja asettele kattilaan.
Survo mausteet ja sipuli, lisää viini, kalakastike, etikka ja öljy ja kaada vihannesten päälle.
Hauduta lähes kypsiksi ja suurusta. Ripottele timjamia ja pippuria.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
[any kind of vegetables or herbs] blanched off in water with [a little] soda; squeeze [out the water] arrange in a saucepan. Grind pepper, lovage, coriander, satury, onion with wine, broth, vinegar and oil; add [this] to the vegetables, stew [all until nearly done] and tie with roux. Sprinkle with thyme, finely ground pepper and serve. Any kind of vegetable [2] may be prepared in the above manner, if you wish.

Selityksiä (Pegge 1780):

[1] Wanting in Tac. and Tor. G.-V. patellam ex holisatro. [2] It is worth noting that Tor. and Tac. omit this recipe entirely and that Tor. concludes the preceding formula with the last sentence of the above formula, except for the difference in one word. Tor. et de quacunque libra [List. et al. herba] si volueris facies ut demonstratum est suprà. This might mean that it is optional (in the preceding formula) to shape the fish into one pound loaves instead of the small fish balls, which is often done in the case of forcemeats, as in veal, beef, ham loaves, or fish pie. We are inclined to accept the reading of Torinus, for the above way of preparing "any kind of vegetables or herbs" is somewhat farfetched. Furthermore, the vegetable dish would more properly belong in Book III. Just another example of where readings by various editors are different because of the interpretations of one word. In this case one group reads libra whereas the other reads herba.

recipes.title: Sardiinimunakas viinikastikkeella
recipes.originalTitle: A dish of sardines (PATELLA DE APUA)
recipes.description: Puolet sardiineista sekoitetaan munien kanssa, loput lisätään hyytyvään munakkaaseen, joka käännetään ja tarjotaan viinikastikkeen kanssa.
instructions: Vatkaa munat ja sekoita joukkoon puolet sardiineista, liemi, viini ja öljy.
Kypsennä pannulla miedolla lämmöllä ja lisää loput sardiinit, kun munakas alkaa hyytyä.
Käännä varovasti, kaada päälle lämmin viinikastike ja ripottele pippuria.
recipes.author: Apicius; engl. J. D. Vehling (1936)
recipes.originalText:
